title: The Principles of Quantum Entanglement
text:
Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, regardless of the physical distance separating them. Measuring a property (such as spin or polarization) on one particle instantaneously determines the corresponding property of the other entangled particles. This correlation famously led Einstein to label it 'spooky action at a distance.'

Mathematically, entanglement indicates that the combined state of the system cannot be described by independent states for each component particle. The particles must be treated as a single quantum entity until measurement occurs. The strength and nature of this link are key resources being explored in developing advanced computing technologies.

Entanglement is crucial to the theoretical foundations of quantum computation and cryptography, promising revolutionary improvements over classical communication methods through protocols like Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).
